name: Internal jugular vein
function: Main venous drainage of the brain, face and neck. Begins at the jugular bulb as the continuation of the sigmoid sinus and ends by joining the subclavian vein to form the brachiocephalic vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Continuation of sigmoid sinus at jugular foramen (superior bulb); receives inferior petrosal sinus, pharyngeal, common facial, lingual, superior and middle thyroid veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends in the carotid sheath lateral to ICA then CCA, with vagus nerve posterior between them; runs deep to SCM; inferior bulb has a bicuspid valve

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins subclavian vein behind the sternoclavicular joint to form the brachiocephalic vein (venous angle)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep cervical lymph node chain along its length; ansa cervicalis on its anterior surface; accessory nerve crosses it near the posterior belly of digastric

pearl: Central line: insert at apex of the triangle between the SCM heads, aiming toward the ipsilateral nipple; IJV lies lateral to the carotid. Lemierre syndrome = septic IJV thrombophlebitis (Fusobacterium) after pharyngitis.

name: External jugular vein
function: Superficial vein draining the scalp and face around the ear and the lateral neck; runs on SCM under platysma and empties into the subclavian vein. Less reliable than the IJV for JVP because of its valves.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Union of posterior auricular vein and posterior division of the retromandibular vein near the angle of the mandible, within or just below the parotid

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends obliquely across SCM deep to platysma, pierces the investing fascia in the posterior triangle just above the clavicle

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Subclavian vein; receives posterior external jugular, transverse cervical, suprascapular and anterior jugular veins near its termination

details.label: Relations
details.value: Great auricular nerve runs parallel and posterior to it on SCM; transverse cervical nerve passes forward deep to it; covered by platysma

pearl: Visible EJV distension in a seated patient suggests raised venous pressure, but JVP is read from the IJV. A cut EJV where it pierces the deep fascia is held open and can suck air: venous air embolism.

name: Anterior jugular vein and jugular venous arch
function: Paired superficial veins of the anterior neck that drain the submental and infrahyoid skin; the two sides are joined above the manubrium by the jugular venous arch.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Submental and superficial submandibular veins near the hyoid

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends near the midline superficial to the infrahyoid strap muscles; turns laterally in the suprasternal space (of Burns) deep to SCM

details.label: Drains into
details.value: External jugular vein (or subclavian) at the root of the neck

details.label: Relations
details.value: Jugular venous arch connects right and left anterior jugulars in the suprasternal space just above the sternal notch

pearl: The jugular venous arch and anterior jugular veins lie in the path of a low tracheostomy or suprasternal incision; identify and ligate them to avoid troublesome bleeding.

name: Posterior external jugular vein
function: Drains the skin and superficial muscles of the occipital scalp and upper back of the neck, running between splenius and trapezius, then joins the external jugular vein just below the middle of its course.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Superficial veins of the occipital scalp and posterior neck (communicates with occipital vein)

details.label: Course
details.value: Begins in the occipital region, descends in the back of the neck between splenius capitis and trapezius, then emerges onto SCM to join the EJV

details.label: Drains into
details.value: External jugular vein just below the middle of its course (about mid-SCM level), not in the lower third

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep to trapezius and superficial to splenius in the upper neck; near the lesser occipital nerve and cutaneous branches of the cervical plexus

pearl: Small tributary that bleeds freely in posterior triangle procedures (lymph node biopsy); of little hemodynamic consequence but easily mistaken for the EJV.

name: Subclavian vein
function: Continuation of the axillary vein draining the upper limb; passes behind the clavicle and joins the IJV to form the brachiocephalic vein. A major central venous access route.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Continuation of axillary vein at the outer border of the first rib; receives external jugular vein and, at its union with the IJV, the thoracic duct (left) or right lymphatic duct

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs medially behind the clavicle, anterior to the anterior scalene muscle and phrenic nerve, over the first rib; separated from the subclavian artery by anterior scalene

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins IJV behind the sternoclavicular joint to form the brachiocephalic vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Pleural apex and subclavian artery lie posterior; valves near its termination

pearl: Infraclavicular line: needle under the clavicle at the junction of its medial and middle thirds, aimed at the sternal notch. Lowest infection rate but highest pneumothorax risk; non-compressible, so avoid in coagulopathy, and avoid in CKD (stenosis would jeopardize a future AV fistula).

name: Brachiocephalic veins
function: Formed by the IJV and subclavian vein on each side; right and left unite to form the SVC. Receive the vertebral, inferior thyroid and internal thoracic veins from the neck.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: IJV + subclavian vein at the venous angle; tributaries: vertebral, inferior thyroid, internal thoracic, first posterior intercostal, (left) superior intercostal

details.label: Course
details.value: Right is short (~2.5 cm) and vertical; left is longer (~6 cm), crosses the midline behind the manubrium and in front of the arch branches to join the right

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior vena cava, behind the first right costal cartilage

details.label: Relations
details.value: Left brachiocephalic vein lies anterior to the brachiocephalic trunk and left common carotid; thymus and manubrium anterior

pearl: The left brachiocephalic vein may lie above the sternal notch in children, placing it at risk during tracheostomy. It is compressed by mediastinal masses in SVC syndrome.

name: Venous angle (jugulo-subclavian junction)
function: Junction of the IJV and subclavian vein behind the sternoclavicular joint, where the brachiocephalic vein begins. The thoracic duct (left) and right lymphatic duct enter here.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: IJV meeting the subclavian vein; receives the thoracic duct on the left and the right lymphatic duct on the right

details.label: Course
details.value: Lies behind the medial end of the clavicle and sternoclavicular joint, anterior to the anterior scalene and phrenic nerve

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Brachiocephalic vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Right vagus crosses anterior to the first part of the right subclavian artery just posterior to the angle (right recurrent laryngeal hooks under the artery); the left vagus descends between the left common carotid and subclavian arteries and crosses the aortic arch (left recurrent laryngeal hooks under the arch); the thoracic duct arches over the left subclavian artery to reach the angle

pearl: Injury to the thoracic duct at the left venous angle (neck dissection, left subclavian line) causes chylous leak or chylothorax; the left supraclavicular Virchow node sits nearby.

name: Facial vein
function: Principal vein of the face, draining the forehead, eyelids, nose, lips and cheek. It is valveless and connects the cavernous sinus to the neck, a route for infection spread.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Begins as the angular vein at the medial canthus; receives deep facial vein (from pterygoid plexus), superior and inferior labial, external nasal and submental veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs obliquely down and back, behind the facial artery, deep to zygomaticus muscles, crosses the mandible at the anterior border of masseter, then over the submandibular gland

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins anterior division of retromandibular vein to form the common facial vein, ending in the IJV

details.label: Relations
details.value: Valveless; communicates with cavernous sinus via superior ophthalmic vein and via deep facial vein and pterygoid plexus

pearl: Danger triangle (nose to angles of mouth): squeezing a furuncle can push infected thrombus via valveless angular and ophthalmic veins into the cavernous sinus, causing cavernous sinus thrombosis.

name: Angular vein
function: Beginning of the facial vein at the medial canthus, formed by the supratrochlear and supraorbital veins; it communicates directly with the superior ophthalmic vein and cavernous sinus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Union of supratrochlear and supraorbital veins at the root of the nose; receives palpebral and external nasal veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs obliquely down the side of the nose along the nasomaxillary groove, lateral to the angular artery, to the level of the inferior orbital margin

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Continues as the facial vein; connects to the superior ophthalmic vein through the orbit

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies about 8 mm medial to the medial canthus; no valves

pearl: Infections of the upper lip, nose or medial canthus can propagate retrograde through the angular vein into the cavernous sinus; look for ophthalmoplegia (CN III, IV, VI), chemosis and fever.

name: Superior and inferior ophthalmic veins
function: Valveless orbital veins draining the eyeball, orbit and eyelids backward into the cavernous sinus, with anterior connections to the angular/facial vein and inferior connections to the pterygoid plexus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Superior: from the angular vein at the medial canthus, receives vorticose, central retinal and ethmoidal veins. Inferior: plexus on the orbital floor

details.label: Course
details.value: Superior ophthalmic vein runs back with the ophthalmic artery, crosses the optic nerve and passes through the superior orbital fissure

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Cavernous sinus (both); the inferior ophthalmic vein also sends a branch through the inferior orbital fissure to the pterygoid plexus

details.label: Relations
details.value: No valves, so blood flows either way depending on pressure

pearl: Carotid-cavernous fistula causes arterialized flow into the superior ophthalmic vein: pulsatile proptosis, chemosis, orbital bruit. A dilated superior ophthalmic vein on CT/MRI is the classic sign.

name: Deep facial vein
function: Short connecting vein running from the pterygoid venous plexus forward over the buccinator to the facial vein, linking the superficial face to the deep infratemporal veins and indirectly to the cavernous sinus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Arises from the anterior part of the pterygoid venous plexus in the infratemporal fossa

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes forward and downward deep to the masseter and ramus, across the buccinator, under the zygomaticus muscles

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Facial vein at about the level of the angle of the mouth / anterior border of masseter

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies near the buccal branch of the facial nerve and the parotid duct; valveless

pearl: Second route from face to cavernous sinus: facial vein to deep facial vein to pterygoid plexus to emissary veins of the foramen ovale. Explains cavernous sinus thrombosis after cheek or dental infections.

name: Pterygoid venous plexus
function: Network of veins in the infratemporal fossa between the pterygoid muscles that drains the structures supplied by the maxillary artery (teeth, palate, nasal cavity, muscles of mastication, dura).

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Veins accompanying maxillary artery branches: sphenopalatine, deep temporal, pterygoid, masseteric, buccal, inferior alveolar, middle meningeal, palatine

details.label: Course
details.value: Lies between temporalis and lateral pterygoid and between the two pterygoid muscles, around the maxillary artery

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Maxillary vein (to retromandibular vein); communicates with facial vein via deep facial vein, with cavernous sinus via emissary veins of foramen ovale and with inferior ophthalmic vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lateral pterygoid muscle, mandibular nerve branches, maxillary artery

pearl: Posterior superior alveolar nerve block or a misplaced needle can pierce the plexus causing a rapidly expanding cheek hematoma. Infections here can track to the cavernous sinus through the foramen ovale.

name: Maxillary vein
function: Short vein that drains the pterygoid venous plexus backward behind the neck of the mandible, where it joins the superficial temporal vein to form the retromandibular vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Confluence of veins from the posterior part of the pterygoid venous plexus (the plexus also drains forward into the facial vein via the deep facial vein)

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs posteriorly with the first part of the maxillary artery between the sphenomandibular ligament and the neck of the mandible

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins the superficial temporal vein within the parotid gland to form the retromandibular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies with the maxillary artery deep (medial) to the mandibular neck; auriculotemporal nerve nearby

pearl: Drains the pterygoid plexus, linked to the cavernous sinus via emissary veins (foramen ovale, foramen lacerum), so facial/dental infection can cause cavernous sinus thrombosis; torn by displaced condylar neck fractures.

name: Retromandibular vein
function: Formed in the parotid gland by union of the superficial temporal and maxillary veins; it splits into an anterior division (to the facial vein) and a posterior division (to the external jugular vein).

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Superficial temporal vein + maxillary vein just behind the neck of the mandible; receives parotid and transverse facial veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends within the parotid gland, superficial to the external carotid artery and deep to the facial nerve branches

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Anterior division joins the facial vein to form the common facial vein (to IJV); posterior division joins the posterior auricular vein to form the external jugular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Parotid gland layers from superficial to deep: facial nerve, retromandibular vein, external carotid artery

pearl: Surgical landmark in parotidectomy: the facial nerve lies just superficial to the retromandibular vein, so the vein marks the plane separating the superficial from the deep lobe of the gland.

name: Common facial vein
function: Short trunk formed by the facial vein and the anterior division of the retromandibular vein below the angle of the mandible; it carries most facial venous blood into the internal jugular vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Facial vein + anterior division of retromandibular vein, just below the angle of the mandible; often receives the lingual and superior thyroid veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Begins just below the angle of the mandible and runs downward and backward across the carotid bifurcation, deep to platysma, to end in the internal jugular vein; the superficial crossing of the submandibular gland is by the facial vein itself, before the union

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Internal jugular vein at about the level of the hyoid bone

details.label: Relations
details.value: Crosses superficial to the carotid bifurcation and hypoglossal nerve; the jugulodigastric lymph node lies close to its termination

pearl: Encountered early in carotid endarterectomy: the common facial vein is divided to expose the carotid bifurcation and the hypoglossal nerve lying just above it.

name: Superficial temporal vein
function: Drains the lateral scalp and temple, descending in front of the tragus to enter the parotid and join the maxillary vein, forming the retromandibular vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Frontal and parietal tributaries from the scalp network; receives middle temporal and transverse facial veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends over the zygomatic arch anterior to the tragus with the superficial temporal artery and auriculotemporal nerve, enters the parotid

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins maxillary vein in the parotid to form the retromandibular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies with the auriculotemporal nerve behind the superficial temporal artery; anastomoses freely with supraorbital and posterior auricular veins

pearl: Scalp lacerations over the temple bleed heavily because the richly anastomotic veins and arteries are held open by the dense connective tissue layer; direct pressure and suturing stop it.

name: Posterior auricular vein
function: Drains the scalp behind the ear and the auricle, descending behind the auricle to join the posterior division of the retromandibular vein and form the external jugular vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Plexus of the scalp behind the ear; receives stylomastoid and auricular veins and the mastoid emissary vein

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends behind the auricle over the mastoid process and the upper SCM

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins the posterior division of the retromandibular vein below the parotid to form the external jugular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Accompanies the posterior auricular artery; the mastoid emissary vein connects it to the sigmoid sinus

pearl: Mastoid emissary vein links the posterior auricular vein to the sigmoid sinus, so mastoiditis or postauricular infection can lead to sigmoid sinus thrombosis.

name: Occipital vein
function: Drains the posterior scalp, running with the occipital artery to the suboccipital region, where it joins the suboccipital plexus and vertebral vein or the posterior auricular/internal jugular veins.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Scalp venous plexus over the occiput; receives the parietal emissary and occipital diploic veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends with the occipital artery, pierces trapezius, enters the suboccipital triangle

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Suboccipital venous plexus and vertebral vein, or posterior auricular vein / IJV (variable)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Greater occipital nerve accompanies it in the scalp

pearl: Occipital scalp lacerations bleed profusely from this vein and the occipital artery; the parietal and occipital emissary veins allow scalp infection to reach the superior sagittal and transverse sinuses.

name: Lingual vein
function: Drains the tongue and floor of the mouth; the dorsal lingual veins accompany the lingual artery and the deep lingual (ranine) vein runs with the hypoglossal nerve, uniting to enter the IJV.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Dorsal lingual veins (with lingual artery), deep lingual vein of the tongue tip, sublingual vein

details.label: Course
details.value: Deep lingual vein runs back on the underside of the tongue, visible through the mucosa, then with the hypoglossal nerve (vena comitans nervi hypoglossi) over hyoglossus

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Internal jugular vein, directly or via the common facial vein, at the level of the hyoid

details.label: Relations
details.value: Hypoglossal nerve, hyoglossus muscle, greater horn of hyoid

pearl: Sublingual drug absorption (nitroglycerin) is rapid because the deep lingual veins drain into the IJV and bypass first-pass hepatic metabolism.

name: Supraorbital and supratrochlear veins
function: Drain the forehead and anterior scalp downward to the medial canthus, where they unite to form the angular vein; the supraorbital vein also communicates with the superior ophthalmic vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Anterior scalp venous network; supraorbital vein also receives the frontal diploic vein

details.label: Course
details.value: Supratrochlear descends near the midline of the forehead; supraorbital runs medially along the orbital rim, sending a branch through the supraorbital notch to the superior ophthalmic vein

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Unite at the medial canthus to form the angular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Accompany the supratrochlear and supraorbital nerves and arteries

pearl: Forehead cellulitis or an infected scalp wound can reach the cavernous sinus through the supraorbital-superior ophthalmic connection; the frontal diploic vein links them to the bone and dural sinuses.

name: Superior thyroid vein
function: Drains the upper pole of the thyroid lobe, accompanying the superior thyroid artery to end in the internal jugular vein (or common facial vein).

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Veins of the upper pole of the thyroid lobe; receives superior laryngeal and cricothyroid veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs upward and laterally with the superior thyroid artery across the external carotid region

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Internal jugular vein, or via the common facial vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: External branch of superior laryngeal nerve runs close to the superior pole vessels

pearl: Ligate the superior pole vessels close to the gland during thyroidectomy to spare the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (cricothyroid), whose injury causes loss of high pitch.

name: Middle thyroid vein
function: Short, often single vein draining the lateral surface of the thyroid lobe directly into the internal jugular vein; it has no accompanying artery.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Veins from the lateral and inferior part of the thyroid lobe

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes laterally across the common carotid artery at the level of the cricoid

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Internal jugular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies anterior to the common carotid artery; tethers the thyroid lobe to the IJV

pearl: The middle thyroid vein must be divided early when mobilizing the thyroid lobe medially; avulsion from the IJV causes brisk bleeding or air embolism.

name: Inferior thyroid veins
function: Several veins from the lower poles and isthmus that form a plexus in front of the trachea and descend behind the manubrium to the brachiocephalic veins; they do not follow the inferior thyroid artery.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Pretracheal venous plexus from the isthmus and lower poles; receive inferior laryngeal, tracheal and esophageal veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Descend on the front of the trachea behind the strap muscles, through the suprasternal region into the superior mediastinum, often uniting as a common trunk

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Left vein into the left brachiocephalic vein; right vein into the right brachiocephalic vein (or at its junction with the SVC)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lie in front of the trachea below the isthmus and are crossed in tracheostomy; a thyroid ima artery (about 10%) may ascend among them

pearl: Bleeding risks in tracheostomy and thyroidectomy: inferior thyroid veins, thyroid ima artery and jugular venous arch lie in front of the trachea below the isthmus; stay midline, open the trachea at rings 2-3, not lower.

name: Vertebral vein
function: Forms as a plexus around the vertebral artery in the transverse foramina of C1-C6, draining the suboccipital region and deep neck muscles, and emerges at C6 to end in the brachiocephalic vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Suboccipital venous plexus and veins from the internal vertebral venous plexus, deep cervical muscles and occipital vein

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends as a plexus around the vertebral artery through the transverse foramina of C1-C6, then as a single vein anterior to the first part of the subclavian artery

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Posterior aspect of the brachiocephalic vein near the venous angle

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep cervical vein joins it; lies anterior to the vertebral artery in the lower neck

pearl: Part of Batson's valveless vertebral venous plexus, linked to the intracranial sinuses via the condylar emissary vein: retrograde flow with raised intrathoracic or abdominal pressure lets prostate and breast cancer seed the vertebrae and skull base, and lets infection spread to the spine or dural sinuses.

name: Vertebral venous plexus (Batson)
function: Valveless network of internal (epidural) and external vertebral veins from skull base to sacrum, communicating with the dural sinuses and the vertebral, intercostal, lumbar and pelvic veins.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Internal plexus in the epidural space (anterior and posterior longitudinal channels) + external plexus around vertebral bodies and arches; basivertebral veins from the bodies

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs the full length of the vertebral canal; communicates superiorly with the basilar and occipital sinuses and the condylar emissary veins

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Vertebral veins (neck), intercostal, lumbar and lateral sacral veins; thus links the caval and azygos systems with the pelvic (prostatic, vesical) venous plexuses

details.label: Relations
details.value: No valves, so flow reverses with raised intrathoracic or intra-abdominal pressure (coughing, straining, Valsalva)

pearl: Batson plexus explains hematogenous spread of prostate (and breast) cancer to the vertebral bodies and skull without lung metastases, and spread of pelvic/urinary infection to the spine (vertebral osteomyelitis, epidural abscess).

name: Cavernous sinus
function: Paired trabeculated dural venous sinus on each side of the sella turcica that drains the orbit, face and brain and surrounds the ICA and cranial nerves III, IV, V1, V2 and VI.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Superior and inferior ophthalmic veins, superficial middle cerebral vein, sphenoparietal sinus, central retinal vein; connects to pterygoid plexus via emissary veins of foramen ovale

details.label: Course
details.value: Lies lateral to the sella and sphenoid body, from the superior orbital fissure to the petrous apex; the two sides join via intercavernous sinuses around the pituitary

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior petrosal sinus (to transverse sinus) and inferior petrosal sinus (to IJV at jugular foramen); basilar plexus

details.label: Relations
details.value: ICA and abducens nerve (VI) run through the sinus; III, IV, V1 and V2 lie in its lateral wall; pituitary medial, temporal lobe lateral

pearl: Cavernous sinus thrombosis (sinusitis, danger-triangle/orbital infection): fever, headache, proptosis/chemosis, ophthalmoplegia (VI first), V1/V2 numbness; often bilateral. IV anti-staph antibiotics; usually add heparin.

name: Superior sagittal sinus
function: Midline dural sinus in the attached border of the falx cerebri, running from the crista galli to the confluence; it receives superior cerebral veins and is the main site of CSF absorption via arachnoid granulations.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Superior cerebral (bridging) veins, diploic and parietal emissary veins; lateral venous lacunae containing arachnoid granulations

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs backward in the midline groove of the skull vault from the foramen cecum to the internal occipital protuberance, widening posteriorly

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Confluence of sinuses, usually continuing as the right transverse sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Bridging veins enter it against the direction of flow; parietal emissary veins connect it to the scalp

pearl: Torn bridging veins entering the sinus cause subdural hematoma (elderly, alcoholics, shaken infants). Sinus thrombosis (OCPs, pregnancy/postpartum, thrombophilia): headache, seizures, papilledema; diagnose with MR/CT venography and anticoagulate even if hemorrhagic.

name: Transverse and sigmoid sinuses
function: Paired sinuses carrying blood from the confluence laterally along the tentorium (transverse) and then in an S-shaped groove on the mastoid (sigmoid) to the jugular foramen, where the IJV begins.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Transverse: from the confluence, receives superior petrosal sinus, inferior cerebral and cerebellar veins. Sigmoid: continuation of transverse, receives mastoid and condylar emissary veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Transverse sinus runs laterally in the attached margin of the tentorium cerebelli; sigmoid curves down and medially behind the mastoid antrum to the jugular foramen

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior bulb of the internal jugular vein at the jugular foramen

details.label: Relations
details.value: Right transverse sinus is usually the larger, continuing the superior sagittal sinus; sigmoid sinus lies just behind the mastoid air cells and the facial nerve canal

pearl: Mastoiditis or otitis media can erode into the sigmoid sinus causing septic lateral sinus thrombosis (Griesinger sign: mastoid edema). The sinus is at risk in mastoidectomy and posterior fossa craniotomy.

name: Confluence of sinuses (torcular herophili)
function: Dilated junction at the internal occipital protuberance where the superior sagittal, straight and occipital sinuses meet and divide into the two transverse sinuses.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Superior sagittal sinus, straight sinus, occipital sinus

details.label: Course
details.value: Lies against the internal occipital protuberance, deep to the inion

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Right and left transverse sinuses (commonly superior sagittal to right, straight to left; often asymmetric)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Attachment of falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli; occipital bone posteriorly

pearl: A suboccipital craniotomy or a depressed fracture over the inion can lacerate the confluence, producing torrential venous bleeding; asymmetric transverse sinuses are common and must not be mistaken for thrombosis.

name: Straight sinus and great cerebral vein (of Galen)
function: Great cerebral vein collects the deep cerebral veins (internal cerebral and basal veins) draining thalamus and basal ganglia; with the inferior sagittal sinus it forms the straight sinus, which runs to the confluence.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Great cerebral vein = union of the two internal cerebral veins, receiving the basal veins of Rosenthal; straight sinus = great cerebral vein + inferior sagittal sinus

details.label: Course
details.value: Great cerebral vein curves up behind the splenium; straight sinus runs posteroinferiorly in the junction of the falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Confluence of sinuses, usually continuing as the left transverse sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Great cerebral vein lies in the quadrigeminal cistern above the pineal gland and superior colliculi

pearl: Vein of Galen malformation in neonates causes high-output heart failure, cranial bruit and hydrocephalus. Deep cerebral venous thrombosis causes bilateral thalamic edema with depressed consciousness.

name: Emissary veins
function: Valveless veins passing through skull foramina to connect the extracranial scalp and face veins with the intracranial dural sinuses; they equalize pressure but allow infection to spread inward.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Parietal (scalp to superior sagittal sinus), mastoid (posterior auricular to sigmoid sinus), condylar (suboccipital plexus to sigmoid sinus), foramen ovale (pterygoid plexus to cavernous sinus), occipital

details.label: Course
details.value: Pass through the parietal foramen, mastoid foramen, condylar canal, foramen ovale, foramen lacerum and foramen cecum

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Dural venous sinuses from the scalp, face and pterygoid plexus; flow may reverse

details.label: Relations
details.value: Connect the loose areolar (danger) layer of the scalp to the sinuses

pearl: Infection in the loose connective tissue layer of the scalp spreads via emissary veins to the dural sinuses and meninges (osteomyelitis, sinus thrombosis, meningitis); hence the scalp 'danger area'.

name: Diploic veins
function: Thin-walled, valveless veins within the cancellous diploe of the skull vault (frontal, anterior and posterior temporal, occipital) that drain into both the dural sinuses and the scalp/pericranial veins.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Frontal diploic vein, anterior and posterior temporal diploic veins, occipital diploic vein, each draining a region of the vault

details.label: Course
details.value: Run in channels within the diploe between the inner and outer tables of the skull

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Inward to the superior sagittal, sphenoparietal, transverse sinuses; outward to supraorbital, deep temporal and occipital veins

details.label: Relations
details.value: Become prominent on skull X-ray as branching lucencies; connect with emissary veins

pearl: Osteomyelitis of the frontal bone from sinusitis (Pott puffy tumor) spreads via diploic veins to cause subperiosteal abscess, epidural abscess and superior sagittal sinus thrombosis.

name: Scalp veins
function: Richly anastomotic superficial scalp veins (supratrochlear, supraorbital, superficial temporal, posterior auricular, occipital) in the dense connective tissue layer, linked to dural sinuses by emissary veins.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Network over the vault drained by the supratrochlear, supraorbital, superficial temporal, posterior auricular and occipital veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Lie in the dense subcutaneous connective tissue (layer 2 of SCALP) with the arteries; emissary veins pass from the loose areolar layer (layer 4) through the skull to the sinuses

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Facial vein (anteriorly), retromandibular and external jugular veins (laterally), suboccipital plexus/vertebral vein and IJV via occipital veins (posteriorly)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Walls are held open by dense connective tissue; the loose areolar layer lets blood or pus spread across the vault and into the eyelids (periorbital ecchymosis)

pearl: Scalp wounds bleed profusely because the vessels cannot retract. Subgaleal hematoma or infection in the loose areolar layer spreads over the whole vault into the eyelids, and via emissary veins to the dural sinuses and meninges.

name: Inferior petrosal sinus
function: Main outflow of the cavernous sinus: runs posteroinferiorly along the petro-occipital fissure to the superior bulb of the internal jugular vein at the jugular foramen.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Arises from the posteroinferior cavernous sinus; receives labyrinthine (internal auditory) veins, pontine and medullary veins, and the basilar plexus

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs posteroinferiorly in the groove between the petrous temporal bone and basilar occiput (petro-occipital fissure) to the anterior part of the jugular foramen

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior bulb of the internal jugular vein just below the jugular foramen (sometimes joins the sigmoid sinus or jugular bulb directly)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Traverses the anterior (pars nervosa) compartment of the jugular foramen alongside CN IX; the basilar plexus on the clivus links the two inferior petrosal sinuses

pearl: Bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling (central:peripheral ACTH ratio ≥2 basal, ≥3 after CRH) confirms pituitary Cushing disease vs ectopic ACTH when pituitary MRI is negative or equivocal (<6 mm) in ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome.

name: Superior petrosal sinus
function: Runs along the petrous ridge in the attached margin of the tentorium, connecting the cavernous sinus to the junction of the transverse and sigmoid sinuses; a key channel linking anterior and posterior dural sinuses.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Begins at the posterosuperior cavernous sinus; receives cerebellar, inferior cerebral and tympanic veins, plus the petrosal vein (of Dandy) from the cerebellum/brainstem

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes posterolaterally in the attached edge of the tentorium cerebelli, grooving the superior border of the petrous temporal bone, and arches over the trigeminal root

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Transverse sinus at the point where it turns into the sigmoid sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Crosses above the trigeminal nerve at the petrous apex (Meckel cave) and lies near the superior semicircular canal and arcuate eminence

pearl: Cavernous sinus thrombosis spreads posteriorly via the petrosal sinuses to the transverse/sigmoid sinuses; otitis media/mastoiditis can seed the same path in reverse. Treat with IV antibiotics plus anticoagulation.

name: Bridging (superior cerebral) veins
function: Eight to twelve veins per hemisphere draining the superolateral and medial cortex; they cross the subarachnoid and subdural spaces to empty into the superior sagittal sinus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Converge from cortical pial veins of the frontal, parietal and occipital lobes; the largest is the superior anastomotic vein of Trolard linking to the superficial middle cerebral vein

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascend over the convexity, pierce the arachnoid, traverse the subdural space and enter the dura on the lateral wall of the superior sagittal sinus; posterior veins enter obliquely forward against the direction of flow

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior sagittal sinus (directly or via the lateral venous lacunae), then confluence and transverse sinuses

details.label: Relations
details.value: Unsupported segment in the subdural space is thin-walled and fixed at the sinus, so it tears with acceleration-deceleration or cerebral atrophy that stretches the veins

pearl: Torn bridging veins cause subdural hematoma: crescent-shaped, crosses sutures but not the midline; classic with cerebral atrophy (elderly, alcoholics), anticoagulation, and shaken infants (retinal hemorrhages).

name: Inferior sagittal sinus
function: Small sinus in the free inferior edge of the falx cerebri that drains the medial hemispheres and falx and joins the great cerebral vein of Galen to form the straight sinus, completing the deep venous pathway.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Begins near the junction of the anterior and middle thirds of the falx; receives veins from the falx, corpus callosum, cingulate gyrus and medial surfaces of the hemispheres

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs posteriorly in the posterior half to two-thirds of the free margin of the falx cerebri, above the corpus callosum, enlarging as it goes

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Unites with the great cerebral vein of Galen at the falx-tentorium junction to form the straight sinus, which runs to the confluence of sinuses

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies between the two hemispheres directly above the corpus callosum and pericallosal arteries; the deep system (internal cerebral veins, basal veins, vein of Galen) enters at its termination

pearl: Deep cerebral venous thrombosis (straight sinus, vein of Galen) causes bilateral thalamic edema with coma; suspect with OCPs, pregnancy/puerperium or thrombophilia; confirm with MR/CT venography.
